title: Relative-strength ratio breakout vs the other two pairs, hourly long
ex_ante_rule: Closed 1h candles only; signal at bar close t, order filled at next bar open. Long only, spot, one position, whole allowed balance, no pyramiding, no take-profit. For traded pair X, Y(t) = geometric mean of the 1h closes of the other two pairs among BTC/USDT, ETH/USDT, BNB/USDT (Y = sqrt(close_A * close_B)); the other two pairs are loaded as informative 1h pairs aligned on the same closed candle timestamp. Ratio R(t) = close_X(t) / Y(t). ENTRY at close of bar t when ALL hold: (1) R(t) > SMA(480) of R at t; (2) R(t) is the highest R of the last 120 bars including t (R(t) >= max R over t-119..t); (3) close_X(t) > SMA(480) of close_X at t; (4) no open position; (5) cooldown satisfied. EXIT at close of bar t (executed next open) when R(t) < SMA(48) of R at t, OR close_X(t) < SMA(480) of close_X at t. STOP-LOSS: fixed 6% below entry price (native intrabar stop). COOLDOWN: no re-entry for 12 candles after any exit. No other filters. All SMAs are simple means of completed bars; no recursive indicators. Warm-up: 480 bars (longest lookback SMA(480); the 120-bar high and SMA(48) are shorter); startup_candle_count = 500. Same rule and numbers for BTC, ETH and BNB.

parameters.reference_basket: geometric mean of the other two pairs

rationale: Mechanism: capital rotates between large-cap coins in waves. When one coin starts outperforming the basket, momentum and rotation flows and slow spreading of news across pairs tend to keep that leadership going for days. The counterparty is the holder who sells a leader too early or who underprices persistent leadership. Dividing by the other two pairs removes the common crypto-market direction, so the signal is relative strength, not just market beta; the 480-bar price SMA gate (20 days) keeps the rule long only in an absolute uptrend, which limits the losing streaks of failed breakouts in bear markets. The exit waits for ratio weakness (below its 48-bar mean) so winners can run for days. Expected frequency: the triple condition is restrictive, so roughly 15-40 trades per year per pair (not verified; the rule is fixed ex ante). Leadership runs of days should give gross moves of several percent per trade against a 0.35% base round trip (0.95% stress), but a moderate win rate with the 6% stop is expected. Success criteria are the existing gates (positive net at base and conservative cost, drawdown limit, at least 30 trades per split). The source describes ratio charts and breakouts of ratios as a standard relative-strength tool; it gives no evidence of profitability, so the edge is a hypothesis.
novelty_vs_tried: All tried hypotheses use only the traded pair's own price (breakouts, dips, trend filters, daily rules). This one uses a cross-sectional signal: the pair's price relative to a basket of the other two pairs. CrossPairCatchUp is the nearest family but is a lagged catch-up; this is leadership persistence on a ratio breakout with a ratio-based exit. It is a new family.
data_visible_at_proposal: No price data seen; only the context file (exploration results of earlier hypotheses) and the LuxAlgo ratio-chart page, as of 2026-11-06.
